baseline_high_severity_recheck.evidence: scan() now runs the regex sweep unconditionally; ac result discarded

findings.produced: SecurityKernel::from_config (drops invalid regexes, logs warn per-pattern)
findings.consumer_location: src/sandbox/factory.rs:47 (from_config result consumed; skip count discarded)
findings.rationale: from_config's doc comment promises 'the factory that wires this kernel in must also surface the skip count to operators', but from_config returns only Self (no count) and factory.rs does not surface anything. Contrast masker.rs install_operator_patterns, which returns (installed, rejected) and is surfaced in start/helpers.rs. Invalid regexes are no longer silent (warn! per pattern), so the residual is only the missing aggregate operator-visible count.
findings.proposed_change: Return (Self, skip_count) from from_config, or add a skip-count accessor; have factory.rs log 'installed N custom patterns, dropped M invalid' when M>0.
findings.risk: A mistyped custom_blocked rule silently fails to apply (fail-open for that rule) with no operator-visible summary; only a warn! in the log tail.
findings.verification: grep from_config / install_operator_patterns; note masker surfaces rejections, kernel does not

findings.rationale: After requires_approval/is_auto_safe were removed, is_blocked has zero production callers (resilience::RiskLevel and secrets::LeakDetector::is_blocked are unrelated types). Safe/Caution are never produced by assess_custom (returns Blocked/Danger/None) and never consumed. The enum derives Ord solely for a self-test.
findings.proposed_change: Delete is_blocked; either delete Safe/Caution or keep them behind a documented 'ordered scale reserved for future' with a #[allow(dead_code)] note.
findings.risk: Dead predicate invites a future caller to trust a semantics that no code path exercises.
findings.verification: grep 'exec::RiskLevel' / 'RiskLevel::' across src — only security_kernel_hook.rs matches Blocked/Danger

findings.rationale: register_pending still invokes cleanup_expired on every new registration, making the write-lock hold O(N) per registration (O(N*R) under concurrency). Liveness filtering (is_live) mitigates the correctness impact but not the lock-stall amplifier. The comment now acknowledges 'bounded work'.
findings.proposed_change: Replace opportunistic sweep with a periodic/tokio interval sweep, or an expiry-time heap; or at minimum skip the sweep when the map is below a threshold.
findings.risk: Many concurrent approval raises stall the pending write lock, delaying resolve_for_session and unrelated callers.
findings.verification: grep cleanup_expired — only caller is register_pending:341

findings.consumer_location: src/exec/masker.rs:44 (mask) and leak detector (not registered as a leak pattern)
findings.rationale: Unchanged from baseline. The pattern has no anchor and matches random dot-separated id triples, causing over-redaction. Note the Discord pattern is only in the masker list, NOT in leak_detector_assets prefixes/patterns — so the leak detector never flags Discord tokens while the masker redacts them (an asymmetry between the two consumers).
findings.proposed_change: Anchor the pattern (e.g. require word boundary + known-length body) and add a matching entry to leak_detector_assets, or drop Discord detection entirely.
findings.risk: Over-redaction of legitimate identifiers; Discord tokens escape the leak detector (Block path) entirely.
findings.verification: grep '[MN][A-Za-z' secret_patterns.rs — present in masker list only, absent from leak_detector_assets

findings.rationale: TOCTOU unchanged from baseline: between analysis and execution a symlink can be swapped at the same path, so the 'found' label and resolved_path are advisory only. The sandbox driver does authoritative resolution, so this is documentation-level risk, but the analysis result still reports 'found'.
findings.proposed_change: Annotate resolution as advisory, or resolve the canonical path once and reuse it at execution.
findings.risk: A stale 'found' + resolved_path can mislead a consumer that trusts the analysis to route/allowlist a binary.
findings.verification: read parser.rs:371-415 — three path.exists() call sites

findings.rationale: Unchanged from baseline: a pre-epoch wall clock (NTP misconfig, VM resume) collapses timestamps to 0, making every approval instant-expire. unwrap_or_default() silently converts the None error case to 0 ms.
findings.proposed_change: Use a monotonic source for expiry (Instant) as the manager already does for created_at, or treat a pre-epoch clock as a hard failure.
findings.risk: Approval prompts auto-timeout in a degraded-clock scenario.

findings.rationale: Expired live-but-not-resolved entries linger in the HashMap (and their oneshot senders) until the next register_pending. is_live() filtering hides them from list_pending/get_pending/resolve_for_session, so the leak is bounded but real for long-idle sessions.
findings.proposed_change: Add a periodic sweep (tokio interval) or drop-on-access; otherwise document the bounded-lifetime guarantee.
findings.risk: Unbounded memory growth for sessions that raise many approvals then go idle.

findings.consumer_location: src/exec/manager.rs:829 (list_pending sorts by record.created_at_ms: wall clock)
findings.rationale: Two FIFO contracts remain: resolve_for_session orders by monotonic Instant; list_pending orders by wall-clock created_at_ms. Under clock skew the 'oldest' card shown to a user (list_pending) can disagree with the card a bare /approve would resolve (resolve_for_session).
findings.proposed_change: Pick one clock for both orders (prefer Instant), or sort list_pending by the same created_at:Instant.
findings.risk: A user sees card A as position 1 but a bare reply resolves card B under clock skew.
findings.verification: read manager.rs resolve_for_session live sort vs list_pending sort

findings.consumer_location: src/security/runtime_guard.rs:234,418 (has_warnings) — but no pattern ever produces Warn
findings.rationale: leak_detector_assets only assigns Block/Redact; Warn is never produced, so has_warnings() is always false at runtime. The consumer is wired but its input is an empty set — an aspirational variant kept for a future policy.
findings.proposed_change: Remove Warn and has_warnings, or add a real Warn-tier pattern; do not leave the always-false consumer.
findings.risk: A future contributor assumes has_warnings() is a live signal and builds warn-and-pass logic that never fires.
findings.verification: grep 'LeakAction::Warn' — only the match in has_warnings()

findings.rationale: The prefix-gate fix made the automaton's only use a discarded is_match(). The struct keeps the field 'for future use', paying build cost (and the .expect panic on construction) for a result nobody reads. dead_code lints won't flag it because the field is technically read.
findings.proposed_change: Remove ac, the prefixes input, and the builder; simplify LeakDetector::new/default_patterns. Reintroduce Aho-Corasick only when a real consumer lands.
findings.risk: Dead scaffolding plus a construction-time panic path that the 'for future use' comment justifies but nothing needs.
findings.verification: read leak_detector.rs scan() — is_match result assigned to _

findings.consumer_location: none found in production (only tests: action.rs:448, analysis.rs:225)
findings.rationale: The one production consumer cited in the baseline (action.rs:269) has moved into a #[test] (action.rs:448). executables() is now test-only; its borrowed Vec<&str> shape forces clones for any would-be caller.
findings.proposed_change: Delete executables() (or move it into the test module). Keep CommandResolution/CommandSegment which are serde-serialized into records.
findings.risk: Dead public API; grepping before deletion is safe — no non-test consumer.

findings.produced: Two types named ApprovalRequest: decision::ApprovalRequest (= ExecApprovalRequest alias) and approval::types::ApprovalRequest (serde tagged enum)
findings.rationale: exec::ApprovalRequest (the struct alias) and exec::approval::types::ApprovalRequest (the wire enum) coexist. Both are consumed, but the shared name is a drift trap: a future import of crate::exec::ApprovalRequest where the wire enum was meant yields the struct and a compile-time type error deep in a different crate.
findings.proposed_change: Rename the wire enum (e.g. ChannelApprovalRequest) or drop the legacy ApprovalRequest alias once callers move to ExecApprovalRequest.
findings.risk: Name-drift (form 5) confusion on the approval seam; no runtime defect today.
findings.verification: grep 'ApprovalRequest' — two distinct defs, both exported

summary: The review-fix worktree has resolved all critical/high findings from exec.md: group-chat approval bypass (originator gate end-to-end), the Aho-Corasick prefix-gate secret leak (regex now unconditional), matched_text secret exposure (removed), the dead Capability/TrustStage/parameter_binding scaffolding (deleted), the regex-on-intent R7/R8/R10 concerns (reframed as advisory, only installed when configured), the parser length-cap DoS (64 KiB guard), and the deny_reason race (liveness guard). Remaining are 12 low/medium findings: two mediums (O(N) cleanup_expired on the register hot path; unanchored Discord regex that also never reaches the leak detector) and ten lows (dead RiskLevel::is_blocked + Safe/Caution, TOCTOU resolve, clock-collapse timestamps, opportunistic-only cleanup, Instant-vs-wallclock FIFO mismatch, dead LeakAction::Warn, dead Aho-Corasick field, test-only executables(), and the duplicate ApprovalRequest name). Most are CUT/DECIDE per the read-before-write rule: no live consumers on the dead branches.
